stories.headline: Apple unveils Siri AI at WWDC with on-device MoE model and Gemini-powered cloud, delayed in EU and China

key_facts.fact: At WWDC 2026 Apple announced a redesigned Siri built on a new Apple Foundation Models architecture, including a Camera-app Siri mode for visual intelligence and a Dynamic Island-based interface.
key_facts.excerpt: At WWDC 2026, Apple is detailing its Apple Intelligence improvements, starting with its Google Gemini collaboration.

key_facts.fact: Apple's on-device Siri stack uses a 3B dense model plus a roughly 20B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 1-4B active parameters, decided once per prompt by early routing.
key_facts.excerpt: @eliebakouch: local models from Apple Siri AI are a 3B dense and a 20B total ~1-4B active (adaptive compute!) for the MoE they use early routing decision to decide once per prompt which experts will be activated

key_facts.fact: Apple Foundation Model Cloud Pro runs on Nvidia GPUs in Private Cloud Compute and is built on Google Gemini foundation models and data, with Apple doing its own pre-training, post-training and RL on top.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple showed off Siri AI demos at its annual WWDC keynote in Cupertino, Calif. ... Apple on Monday revealed what it's been working ... @nvidia: Proud to collaborate on the next frontier of private AI. Apple is expanding Private Cloud Compute to @GoogleCloud using NVIDIA GPUs.

key_facts.fact: Apple says its most powerful on-device AI model requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air, an M4-or-later iPad or an M3-or-later Mac, each with at least 12GB of RAM.
key_facts.excerpt: @shishirshelke1: Most powerful on-device models will be available only on iPhone Air and 17 Pro / Pro Max 12GB RAM is standard for it

key_facts.fact: Siri AI will not ship in the European Union or China when the new features arrive in beta later this year; Apple blamed the EU's DMA in a full-page press release and addressed the China delay in a footnote.
key_facts.excerpt: The new enhanced Siri AI features that Apple announced today at WWDC 2026 will not be available in the European Union or in China when they are released in beta later this year.

key_facts.fact: Apple opened a Foundation Models framework and a new Core AI framework to developers, plus Xcode enhancements aimed at agentic coding workflows.
key_facts.excerpt: @flowritescode: WWDC26 Notes ... FoundationModels custom skills server models Core AI framework connects app intents with foundationmodels

key_facts.fact: Apple announced an Apple Intelligence feature that uses agentic AI to automatically change compromised passwords and store them in the Passwords app.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple unveils an Apple Intelligence feature to automatically change compromised passwords, using agentic AI, and save them to the Passwords app

stories.headline: OpenAI confidentially files S-1 with SEC, joining Anthropic and SpaceX in IPO queue

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced on June 8 that it had recently submitted a confidential S-1 to the SEC and was disclosing the filing because it expected the news to leak.
key_facts.excerpt: We recently submitted a confidential S-1. We expect it to leak so we're just announcing it. We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while because there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI was last valued at more than $850 billion after a $122 billion funding round in March 2026 and had been targeting a potential public debut as soon as Q4 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The artificial intelligence company, which is valued at more than $850 billion, has been gearing up to go public as soon as the fourth quarter of this year.

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the filing process for OpenAI's potential listing.
key_facts.excerpt: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the filing process ahead of a potential fall listing, according to The Wall Street Journal.

key_facts.fact: The filing comes a week after Anthropic submitted its own confidential S-1 on June 1, having closed a $65 billion round at a $965 billion valuation, and days before SpaceX is set to start trading.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic filed its own confidential S-1, roughly a week earlier. Anthropic recently closed a $65 billion round at a valuation of $965 billion. That figure pushed it past OpenAI. SpaceX leads the group. It is targeting a June 12 Nasdaq debut.

key_facts.fact: Investor forecasts reviewed by the WSJ suggest OpenAI's pace of cash consumption would be unprecedented among publicly traded companies; OpenAI has also missed some internal revenue targets while Anthropic has pulled ahead among business customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Investor forecasts reviewed by The Wall Street Journal suggest the pace of OpenAI's cash consumption would be unprecedented among publicly traded companies. OpenAI has also missed some internal revenue targets recently, while Anthropic has pulled ahead among business customers.

stories.headline: Anthropic says Claude Mythos Preview turns disclosed vulnerabilities into working exploits in hours, not weeks

key_facts.fact: Anthropic researchers ran Claude Mythos Preview against 18 Firefox security patches and got 8 working code-execution exploits, with the first exploit produced in under an hour of Mozilla releasing the patch.
key_facts.excerpt: Across 18 recent Firefox security patches, Claude Mythos Preview, our most capable model, built 8 working code-execution exploits autonomously... Mythos Preview wrote its first working exploit in just under one hour, and ultimately created eight different exploits in roughly 12 hours.

key_facts.fact: On 21 Windows kernel patches with no source code available, Mythos Preview produced 18 proof-of-concept crashes (first in 31 minutes, all within six hours) and 8 full exploit chains escalating a low-privilege user to SYSTEM level.
key_facts.excerpt: In testing against 21 Windows kernel vulnerabilities, Mythos Preview developed proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits for 18 vulnerabilities... The model later generated eight exploit chains that elevated a low-privileged user to SYSTEM-level access. It produced its first proof-of-concept in 31 minutes and generated all 18 within six hours.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic estimates the Windows kernel privilege-escalation chains cost roughly $1,700-$2,200 in API credits, averaging about $2,000 per exploit.
key_facts.excerpt: exploits, at a cost of $1,700 in API credits—an average of about $2,000 per privilege escalation. The binding constraint to N-days is now just a few thousand dollars and API access

key_facts.fact: Anthropic concludes that publicly available models with safeguards disabled can also build exploits, though fewer than Mythos Preview, and argues that 'N-day has become dangerously misleading. N-hour is closer to the reality we now operate in.'
key_facts.excerpt: The researchers argued that exploit-development timelines have shortened to the point where the term 'N-day' may no longer accurately reflect the threat. 'N-day has become dangerously misleading. N-hour is closer to the reality we now operate in,' the researchers concluded.

key_facts.fact: For Firefox, the patched stable release was still 18 days away when Mythos Preview produced its first working exploit from the patch diff.
key_facts.excerpt: Mythos Preview had its first exploit within an hour of Mozilla issuing the patch for it—while it would've been 18 days before the patched Firefox 148 was even released.

stories.headline: Cursor hits $4B annualized revenue ahead of expected SpaceX acquisition

key_facts.fact: AI coding startup Cursor passed $4 billion in annualized revenue in the past week, up from $3 billion in April and $2 billion in February, according to a person familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: Cursor, which is prepping for an expected acquisition by SpaceX, passed $4B in annualized revenue in the last week, up from $3B in April and $2B in Feb.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX announced in April 2026 an option to acquire Cursor's parent Anysphere for $60 billion later this year, or pay $10 billion as a breakup fee if it walks away.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX said it has an agreement giving it the right to acquire artificial intelligence startup Cursor for US$60 billion later this year or to pay US$10 billion for the companies' work together

key_facts.fact: As part of the April deal, Cursor is using xAI's Colossus supercomputer for training, with compute described as equivalent to roughly one million H100 GPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: Cursor publicly stated the agreement will let it 'leverage xAI's Colossus infrastructure to dramatically scale up the intelligence of our models.' The compute pairing has been described as equivalent to roughly one million H100 GPUs.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX is deferring the full Cursor acquisition until after its imminent IPO, which is targeting a roughly $1.75 trillion valuation; the deal is structured as a call option to avoid disrupting the listing filings.
key_facts.excerpt: A confirmed Cursor relationship adds an AI moat to the SpaceX prospectus without forcing a $60B charge before the IPO. $10B is a small price for adding an AI chapter to a $1.75T story.

stories.headline: Google orders 3M+ Intel-made TPUs for 2028 as Nvidia tests Intel 18A; Intel jumps 11%

key_facts.fact: Google has placed a firm order with Intel to manufacture more than three million in-house tensor processing units in 2028 after months of testing Intel's packaging technology.
key_facts.excerpt: Google has placed an order with Intel to manufacture more than three million of its in-house tensor processing units in 2028, while Nvidia is evaluating Intel's advanced packaging and its most cutting-edge 18A process for future chips, The Information reported on Monday

key_facts.fact: Morgan Stanley estimates Google will produce more than six million TPUs across 2027 and 2028, meaning Intel's order accounts for roughly half of the projected 2028 output.
key_facts.excerpt: The Bull, citing Morgan Stanley estimates, notes that Google is expected to produce over 6 million TPUs between 2027 and 2028, implying that Intel's foundry order could account for roughly half of its projected 2028 output.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is running early multi-project wafer runs on Intel's 18A process and is testing whether Intel can build a processor that fuses four GPU dies into one, a design tied to Nvidia's next-generation Feynman GPU architecture due in 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has not committed. It is running early trials, including multiproject wafer runs on 18A, and testing whether Intel can build a processor that fuses four graphics chips into one, a design tied to its Feynman GPU architecture due in 2028.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix is also testing whether its high-bandwidth memory works reliably with Intel's advanced packaging.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix is reportedly testing whether its high-bandwidth memory works reliably with Intel's packaging too.

key_facts.fact: Intel shares jumped about 11-12% on the news.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel's shares jumped about 12 per cent on the news.

stories.headline: China drafts $295B five-year plan to build nationwide AI data centers with mostly local chips

key_facts.fact: China is drafting plans to spend $295 billion over the next five years building AI data centers nationwide, according to Bloomberg sources.
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: China is drafting plans to spend $295B over the next five years on building AI data centers, sourcing 80%+ of tech from local suppliers like Huawei

key_facts.fact: More than 80% of the technology in the buildout would come from local suppliers including Huawei, as Beijing accelerates its push for AI self-sufficiency.
key_facts.excerpt: China is drafting plans to spend $295B over the next five years on building AI data centers, sourcing 80%+ of tech from local suppliers like Huawei

key_facts.fact: Separately, a group of Chinese tech companies including Alibaba and memory maker CXMT is launching a roughly $577 million private-equity fund aimed at strengthening China's 'hard tech' sectors amid tightening US export controls.
key_facts.excerpt: A group of Chinese tech companies, including Alibaba and CXMT, launches a ~$577M PE fund to boost China's 'hard tech' sectors amid tightening US export curbs

key_facts.fact: On the same day, the US Department of Defense added Alibaba, BYD and Baidu to its list of Chinese entities deemed to support the Chinese military.
key_facts.excerpt: The US DOD designates some of China's biggest companies, including Alibaba, BYD, and Baidu, as entities that support the Chinese military

stories.headline: Google upgrades NotebookLM with Gemini 3.5, Antigravity and agentic research capabilities

key_facts.fact: Google announced an update to NotebookLM that moves the research tool to Gemini 3.5 as the default model, adds agentic capabilities and introduces new output formats for multi-step research.
key_facts.excerpt: Google on Monday announced an update to its NotebookLM research tool, which includes new features and the shift to Gemini 3.5 as the default model.

key_facts.fact: The upgraded NotebookLM also runs on Antigravity and is being rolled out globally on the web starting with Google AI Ultra users and Workspace business customers with AI Ultra or AI Expanded access.
key_facts.excerpt: @vikaskansalhq: A more powerful NotebookLM with agentic capabilities, more advanced reasoning, and a suite of new output formats rolling out globally on the web starting with Google AI Ultra users first!

key_facts.fact: Google also cut the price of its Google AI Plus plan to $4.99/month from $7.99 and doubled included storage to 400GB.
key_facts.excerpt: Google announced today that its AI Plus subscription is getting a price drop to $4.99 per month and now includes 400 GB of storage.
